quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
rationale: Vendor gives the full preferred indemnity: IP infringement (20.1) plus breach of law, bodily injury/property damage, Customer Data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud (20.2). Procedure in 20.4 is standard, 20.5 provides procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 is narrow (unmodified Customer material and Customer's unlawful use, with Vendor Technology/modification/instruction exclusions). Indemnities also sit outside the liability cap as Excluded Claims.

quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables and shall obtain equivalent assignments from its personnel.
rationale: We own Customer Data and our pre-existing IP (14.1) and each Deliverable, with a present assignment from Vendor and personnel (14.2). Vendor retains only Vendor Technology, backed by the perpetual Section 13.2 licence where embedded (14.3), and 14.4 bars joint ownership and keeps feedback unrestricted for us. The 14.1 "improve the Services" processing right is confined to improving the Services for us and is further constrained by Section 15.1 (no model training or cross-customer combination without consent), so it does not transfer rights in our data.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Matches our preferred position: mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees (paid or payable) and USD 1,000,000; mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 21.2 with incident-response and replacement-service costs preserved as direct damages; Excluded Claims in 21.3 cover confidentiality, data-protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirm payment obligations are not damages. "Fees" (1.5) is a meaningful base of recurring, professional-services and usage fees.

quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
rationale: Preferred position met: we may assign to Affiliates and successors without consent (24.1); Vendor may not assign, delegate or transfer by change of control without our consent and never to a competitor (24.2); and 24.4 bars any Vendor termination, suspension, repricing or fee acceleration on our change of control. Section 24.3's catch-all applies only to "other assignments" and does not cut back 24.1, and Section 13.3 aligns licence transfer with Section 24.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a sole-and-exclusive supplier obligation, and this clause contradicts Sections 2.1 and 12.3, so we have deleted it. If Vendor needs protection we could discuss exclusivity limited to a defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically if Vendor misses service levels.

quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
rationale: Section 2.2 imposes full-term exclusive dealing on us for an entire service category with no performance-based exit — our walk-away position. It also contradicts Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment). We have proposed deleting it, with a narrowed category/12-month/service-level-exit fallback if Vendor needs protection.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not pay liquidated damages or penalties; USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay is punitive and uncapped. We have replaced it with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented additional costs, which is the standard remedy for customer-caused delay.

ops.newText: If Customer materially delays a dependency identified in an Order Form, Vendor is relieved of the affected obligations and dates for the period of delay and may recover its documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs actually incurred as a result. No liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.
ops.oldText: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.

proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable liquidated damages with schedule relief and documented costs.

quote: Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
rationale: Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages on us of USD 25,000 per day triggered by any dependency delay, however minor — our walk-away position, since accrual is unbounded and could exceed the remaining contract value. We have replaced it with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs, and confirmed no penalties are payable by us.

quote: Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer.
rationale: Affiliates and contractors are expressly covered (13.1); paid-up and embedded software carries a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence with modification rights (13.2); licence rights transfer to an Affiliate or successor (13.3); and there is no at-will revocation — suspension is limited to a material uncured breach after notice and cure. The Section 13.4 restrictions are conventional and expressly do not limit authorised security testing or use of Customer Data and output.

quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us; Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to build, buy and compete in any field or territory. The only countervailing restraint is the exclusivity language in Section 2.2, which we have addressed under EXCLUSIVITY.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains no convenience right, which we cannot accept in a three-year term (Section 8.1). We have added a Customer-only termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2; our fallback is 60-90 days' notice.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty or early-termination charge, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination in accordance with Section 10.2. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Insert Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund.

quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
rationale: Section 9 provides only termination for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and our special cause triggers (9.3); there is no termination-for-convenience right anywhere, in a three-year term (Section 8.1). Absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is our walk-away, so we have inserted a new 9.6 giving us 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Audits of our usage must be no more than annual, on 30 days' notice, records-based and conducted by an independent auditor, with no access to our systems. As drafted, unlimited unannounced audits with remote system access is a walk-away and already contradicts the access limits in Section 22.2.

ops.newText: No more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice and during normal business hours, Vendor may engage an independent auditor bound by confidentiality obligations to verify Customer's usage of the Services by reviewing relevant usage records Customer provides. Vendor and its auditor have no right of access to Customer's systems, whether remote or on-site.
ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.

proposal.summary: Limit audits to annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, records only, no system access.

quote: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
rationale: Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems is our walk-away position, and it directly contradicts Section 22.2, which already says Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems. We have limited audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, records-based only and with no system access; the Section 22.2 cost allocation (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meets our position.

rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County is exactly our preferred position, with no arbitration. CISG is excluded, and the Section 28.3 executive escalation expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-period filings.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not give most-favoured-customer undertakings to suppliers, and this clause is inconsistent with Section 12.3, so we have deleted it. MFN pricing running in our favour remains welcome.

quote: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
rationale: The MFN runs the wrong way: it obliges us to extend Vendor the best terms we give any other technology supplier, open-endedly and with no product limit or comparison carve-outs — our walk-away position. It also conflicts with the no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement in Section 12.3. We have proposed deletion.

quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
rationale: Preferred position met: no minimum or take-or-pay commitment, fees are payable only for ordered Services, and non-ordering is expressly not a shortfall. Section 12.3 reinforces that we have given no minimum-volume undertaking, and Section 7.1 bars unlisted minimum-use charges. Residual risk is limited to a commitment appearing in a future Order Form, which we will police at that stage.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept only a mutual, narrow non-solicit: 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire. The 18-month, all-personnel, "engage" restriction binding only us is not acceptable and conflicts with Section 12.3.

ops.newText: For twelve months after a person's involvement in the Services ends, neither Party will knowingly solicit for employment any of the other Party's personnel who were directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertisements or other recruitment not targeted at the other Party's personnel, responses to them, or the hiring of any person who approaches a Party on an unsolicited basis, and neither Party is restricted from hiring any person.
ops.oldText: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.

proposal.summary: Make non-solicit mutual, 12 months, involved personnel only, with carve-outs and no no-hire.

quote: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
rationale: The non-solicit binds only us, runs 18 months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars "engaging" them (an effective no-hire) and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. We have narrowed it to the fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, involved personnel only, with carve-outs and no no-hire.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A 180-day non-renewal window is far longer than we can operate; our position is a 30-day opt-out with a 60-day Vendor reminder (fallback: 60 days). The 12-month renewal term and the Section 8.3 uplift cap of the lesser of CPI and 3% are acceptable.

proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice from 180 to 30 days and add renewal reminder.

quote: Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
rationale: The renewal term (12 months) and the Section 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice) meet our position, but a 180-day non-renewal window exceeds even our walk-away threshold of 90 days. We have shortened the opt-out to 30 days and added a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder; 60 days is our fallback.

rationale: Preferred position met in full: six months' transition assistance including migration and cooperation with a replacement supplier (11.1); return of all Customer Data within 30 days in a documented machine-readable format with metadata and no fee-dispute hostage (11.2); and secure deletion only after we confirm successful return, certified by an officer (11.3). Section 10.1 keys the access cut-off to the end of the agreed transition period, so there is no gap.

quote: Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form. Vendor further warrants that Services and Deliverables will materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
rationale: Meets or exceeds our position: professional and workmanlike services warranty (19.1); 90-day Deliverable conformity running from delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, and hosted Services conformity for the whole subscription term (19.2); no-malicious-code and compliance-with-law warranties (19.3); and a re-perform/repair/replace remedy with a refund and termination backstop that is expressly non-exclusive (19.4). The Section 19.5 disclaimer expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or data-protection duty.
